\begin{remark}[ASV and E-values as complementary tools]
\label{rem:evalue}
ASV diagnostics and E-values~\cite{vanderweele_ding2017} address different bias sources---annotation error vs.\ unmeasured confounding---and are most valuable when used jointly (Table~\ref{tab:sensitivity_comparison}, Appendix).
\emph{(i)~Topology dependence}: ASV captures how the same $C$ has different consequences across topologies; E-values are topology-agnostic.
\emph{(ii)~Sign-flip diagnostic}: sign-flip ASV $\delta^*_{\mathrm{sf}}$ targets a failure mode absent from unmeasured confounding.
\emph{(iii)~Parametric structure}: ASV searches $C(\delta)$ paths in the column-stochastic polytope; E-values optimize over $[1,\infty)$.
In short, ASV answers ``how much annotation error before the effect sign reverses?'' while E-values answer ``how much confounding before the effect disappears?''---orthogonal threats.
\end{remark}

tool_args.command: echo "Large language models are increasingly used as annotators in computational social science, yet annotation errors propagate into downstream causal estimates in ways that depend on both the confusion matrix structure and the causal DAG topology. We derive bias expressions for seven canonical topologies under K-class non-differential misclassification in linear structural equation models and show that K >= 3 introduces a structural possibility of sign reversal absent in the binary case. We prove sign preservation for confounding and collider, and verify it numerically for mediation, M-bias, and front-door; exposure and IV topologies can reverse the treatment effect sign. Under realistic LLM accuracy, sign reversal of non-dominant coefficients occurs under exposure; under empirical LLM matrices (diagonal 0.45--0.81), sign reversal is confined to exposure; IV is fragile under uniform Dirichlet priors but exhibits zero reversals under empirical LLM matrices. We introduce Annotation Sensitivity Values (ASVs), with proved (K=2) and numerically verified (K>=3) monotonicity, yielding a vulnerability ranking from IV (maximally fragile) to M-bias (immune), and show that matrix-based corrections are provably ineffective under linear regression for four topologies due to Frisch--Waugh--Lovell invariance.
